item.title: ComfyUI expands to 779 nodes for image, video, and 3D workflows
item.description:
ComfyUI expands to 779 nodes for image, video, and 3D workflows

ComfyUI has grown to include 779 nodes, expanding its capabilities to handle image, video, 3D, and language models along with the plumbing between them. The project has maintained an MIT license since 2023 and has accumulated over a million downloads. Its architecture is designed so that nothing is installed or fetched unless explicitly requested.

🧩 Core Capabilities

The node library supports a wide range of processing tasks, including:

  • Tiled and affine samplers, noise shaping, shift and schedule control, model quantizing, and LoRA stacks.
  • Crop-and-restore edits, edit regions, and specific model integrations like MiniMax H3 Image, Fibo 2.0, and BluePixel 4K.
  • Raw-style develop, film stocks, darkroom effects, and looks baked into LUTs.
  • Levels, LUTs, ACES and colour spaces, linear light, HDR video, and scopes and charts.
  • Skin, face, and subject masks, including masks drawn directly on the picture and subjects followed through a clip.
  • Filters and optics, layer stacks, layered PSD and TIFF files, and ControlNet preprocessors.

🎬 Video and 3D Features

Recent developments extend ComfyUI’s utility into complex video production and 3D generation:

  • Video Production: The Prompt Timeline allows long videos to be built a segment at a time. Features include upscaling, sparse attention, and Pika H3 Flex integration. The system supports video with sound, video super-resolution of any length, edits, transitions, titles, restored footage, face restoration through a shot, audio mixing, and beats.
  • 3D Generation: Capabilities include scenes, generated models, characters, meshes, blockouts, point cloud worlds, and Video Blueprint.

📚 Text and Logic Tools

The platform also includes utilities for prompt engineering and data handling:

  • Prompt terminology and a style library.
  • A system prompt library.
  • Support for text, lists, and dictionaries.

🚀 Availability and Resources

  • License: MIT (since 2023).
  • Downloads: Over a million.
  • Examples: 144 example workflows are provided.
  • Installation Model: Nothing installed, nothing fetched unless asked.

item.title: ViMax v1.2.0 adds Web UI and new model providers
item.description:
ViMax v1.2.0 adds Web UI and new model providers

ViMax has released version 1.2.0, introducing a Web UI and expanding its support for image, video, and chat model providers. The update also includes stability improvements to its Agent Loop and TUI workflows and the release of a new Novel2Video pipeline.

🔍 Overview

ViMax is an agentic video creation framework that connects narrative planning, visual consistency, image generation, video generation, and final assembly in one extensible workflow. This update focuses on enhancing the user interface and integrating new generation models.

🧩 How it works

The framework operates through a consistent production pipeline that coordinates references, first frames, camera continuity, and final assembly end to end. It also supports parallelized generation, allowing compatible shots and media assets to be generated concurrently to accelerate multi-shot video production.

⚙️ Key details

  • Web UI Features: The new interface supports named projects, Agent Loop conversations, artifact and storyboard previews, render checkpoints, file uploads, provider settings, and dark mode.
  • Agent Loop and TUI: A stability update includes stronger LLM retries, persistent render status, landscape image guards, and Script2Video resume fixes. The Agent Loop and TUI workflow is integrated for interactive planning, revision, rendering control, session reuse, and context compaction.
  • Model Providers: Support added for OpenRouter GPT Image 2 image generation, Seedance 2.0 Fast video generation, Google Omni video generator, and MiniMax chat model.
  • Novel2Video: A new workflow designed to adapt long-form fiction into episodic visual narratives with narrative compression, character tracking, and scene planning.

💡 Capabilities

Workflow Description
Idea2Video Turns a short concept into structured stories, characters, scripts, storyboards, shots, and a finished video.
Script2Video Converts an explicit screenplay into controllable multi-scene, multi-shot video while preserving its creative intent.
Novel2Video Adapts long-form fiction into episodic visual narratives with narrative compression, character tracking, and scene planning.
AutoCameo Places a person or pet from a reference photo into generated stories while maintaining a consistent appearance.

item.title: Convex Integrates Mastra for AI Workflow Development
item.description:
Convex Integrates Mastra for AI Workflow Development

Convex has introduced a new integration with Mastra, enabling developers to build and run AI workflows directly on its hosted backend platform. This integration allows users to create agents, define workflows, and execute them asynchronously using Convex serverless functions, while leveraging Convex’s reactivity, storage, and vector capabilities.

🧩 How it Works

The Mastra component for Convex provides full support for durable workflows, including:

  • Asynchronous execution from serverless functions (mutations or actions)
  • Tracking workflow status via reactive queries
  • Resuming workflows after suspension for user input
  • Step forking, joining, and triggering
  • Storage and vector integrations for agent memory and RAG

To use the component, developers must:

  • Have an existing Convex project
  • Install the @convex-dev/mastra package
  • Manually install and export @libsql/client due to bundling issues
  • Call storage.setCtx(ctx) and vector.setCtx(ctx) before using storage or vector features in actions

⚙️ Key Details

The integration enables:

  • Running workflows from both mastra dev and convex dev for rapid iteration
  • Using Convex for agent memory with storage and vector features
  • Supporting agentic workflows involving user input, multiple LLM calls, and third-party integrations
  • Custom mutation steps for transactional operations with guaranteed completion
  • Helper functions to securely export actions for browser usage

#Convex #Mastra #AIWorkflows #Serverless #Agents

Source: convex/mastra

item.title: Anchor Ventures to Host Panel on AI Agent Workflows for Founders
item.description:
Anchor Ventures to Host Panel on AI Agent Workflows for Founders

Anchor Ventures is hosting a two-part session featuring a panel of founders who have spent the past year building with specialized AI agents to increase shipping pace with lean teams.

⚙️ Key details

Panel Participants

Name Role
Kat Erickson Moderator, Author and Strategist, Tech Confidential: The Insider’s Playbook for Daring Entrepreneurs
Greg Cangialosi Founder and CEO, Twilight Technologies Inc.
Chris White Founder, NexSys Labs
Rob Wray Founder and CEO, TrayVerify

Session Topics

  • Comparison of what a three-person team can ship versus a 15-person team
  • The advantages of a team of agents over a single large agent
  • Current implementations used by founders and their associated costs
  • Available free cloud and startup credits via hyperscaler programs
  • Tasks that cannot be handed off and require human sign-off
  • Managing burnout and the shortening lifespan of technical skills

🚀 Availability

This is the first of two sessions. The second part, “AI Agents in Action: A Live Deep Dive,” will take place on Thursday, October 29, and will feature the live build of an agent workflow.

#AIAgents #Founders #AnchorVentures #AIWorkflows
